checks.finding: Ruling C(1)'s detection-only Registry recheck ('step 6.5') is fully specified only in Data Plan (design.md:643-656) and cross-referenced in Design Decisions (design.md:2329, 'steps 6.5 and 13') and the validate-resolver-evidence contract (design.md:1560), but is never given its own paragraph in the API/Contract Plan's numbered Processing order (design.md:897-1211; steps 5, 6, 7 run in direct sequence with no 6.5 entry) even though that section claims 'Each step's own failure maps to exactly one REQ-002 diagnostic', implying exhaustiveness. design.md's own Exit-codes step enumeration (design.md:1206) omits '6.5' entirely, directly contradicting Design Decisions' own citation of 'steps 6.5 and 13' for the identical snapshot-generation-mismatch diagnostic. The Architecture ASCII diagram (design.md:63-167) shows no box for this recheck between Registry discovery and the evaluate-predicate fan-out either. Separately, design.md's Test Strategy claims 'Items 1-10 below are, in aggregate, the full fixture matrix' (design.md:1780-1785), yet item 2's per-diagnostic fixture list never names the AC-057 (registry-swapped-during-validation) or AC-058 (affected-component-absent-from-context) fixtures -- both are cited only elsewhere in design.md (lines 654-655, 938-939), never inside the section that is the authoring contract for the future Phase-2 test task. None of the four layer specs cite AC-057, AC-058, TEST-057, or TEST-058 anywhere (verified by grep); security-spec.md's B3 row (line 69) narrates ruling C(1) in prose but its AC column lists only AC-040, AC-048, AC-049 (omitting AC-057), and no threat-table row exists for ruling C(2) at all. investigation.md's Rulings C(1)/C(2) record confirms the follow-up commit re-anchored requirements.md only -- design.md is absent from that follow-up's touched-file list. Concrete failure mode: a Phase-2 implementer following design.md's canonical Processing-order/Exit-codes/Test-Strategy sections in isolation risks omitting the step-6.5 recheck and/or its AC-057/AC-058 fixtures, and a security reviewer relying on security-spec.md's threat table alone would miss ruling C(2) entirely.

OQ-001 and OQ-002 (design.md:2760-2775) are each explicitly non-blocking with an identifiable future-owner scope; OQ-003 is resolved in this revision with a concrete file:line-cited anchor and a drift-check fixture (AC-053). No open question blocks implementation without a stated resolution path.

design.md's Assumptions (2749-2758) restate requirements.md's: A1-A4 contracts land unmodified before Phase-2 (issue sequencing, INV-002); the reservation is live in guard-invariants.json (INV-003, with an explicit three-step fallback in the Protected-File Statement); SKILL.md's unprotected status is re-verified at future task start (INV-017). Each assumption cites a specific INV reference or a stated contingency procedure.

design.md's Constraint Compliance (2712-2747) addresses AGENTS.md rules, the hard file-boundary constraint, Security constraints, and Compatibility constraints; requirements.md's Security Boundaries are mirrored by design.md's own section including the C(1)/C(2)-relevant fail-closed/journaled-transaction/crash-recovery guarantees. No requirements.md constraint is contradicted or left unaddressed.
No performance requirements found in requirements.md (grep for response-time/throughput/concurrency/latency/SLA/numeric-threshold keywords returns no match).

Deployment / CI Plan (2677-2710) names the vendored packaging target, the CI pipeline changes (suite registration, staged test.yml human-copy candidate, vendored-copy drift entry), and per-task CHANGELOG discipline. No feature-flag strategy is needed; the protected-path content-population ordering is concretely sequenced in the Protected-File Statement.
Data Plan states Migration Strategy: none (no database, no runtime storage, no schema migration); every new artifact is net-new.

External Integrations states None (2671-2675); the cross-script dependencies on sibling-epic CLIs are internal repository primitives, each individually documented with purpose, contract shape, and failure behaviour across Cross-Layer Dependencies and the API/Contract Plan's numbered steps.

The Components table matches requirements.md's Goals exactly: one script family, one companion validator, one new schema, one documented (not implemented) caller-integration contract; no additional component, data model, or API endpoint beyond REQ-001..REQ-008.

High-risk surfaces (the fail-closed C(1)/C(2) Block conditions; the atomicity/TOCTOU transactional-publication mechanism) each have named validation paths: AC-057's registry-swapped-during-validation fixture (design.md:654-655), AC-058's affected-component-absent-from-context fixture (design.md:938-939), and the TEST-038/039/040/047/048/049 set.
